ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60–80 cm. It is dark brown above with a pale, checkered belly and a distinct yellow nuchal collar. It features 17 rows of strongly keeled midbody scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Nicobar Island Keelback is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, broad yellow or cream-colored nuchal collar that contrasts sharply against its dark body.
ai.habitat: *Hebius nicobariensis* inhabits the humid tropical rainforests and evergreen forests of the Nicobar Islands, typically found near freshwater streams at low elevations.
ai.behavior: The Nicobar Island Keelback is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for frogs and tadpoles in the damp, forested stream environments of its native islands.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hebius nicobariensis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hebius nicobariensis* is endemic to the Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal, occurring at low to moderate elevations within this tropical island biogeographic zone.
